newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Philips considers Lithuania plant - report.
newsitem.headline: Philips considers Lithuania plant - report.

text.p: Dutch electronics giant Philips is considering building a plant in Lithuania to assemble mobile phones and other telecommunications equipment from Western-made components, business newspaper Verslo Zinios said on Friday.

It quoted Philips Projects manager Mike King as saying that the new plant, which would be built near the northern town of Siauliai, would employ between 500 and 2,000 people and assemble products for the market of the former Soviet Union.
"The annual turnover of the Siauliai plant would be between $200 million and $300 million," the newspaper quoted King as saying.
Philips has set as its main condition that the Lithuanian government has to take part in setting up the plant.

The plant would assemble mobile phones, retransmitters and radio apparatus from parts made by Simoco, now partly-owned by Philips but which used to be the wholly-owned Philips Telecom-Private Mobile Radio unit.
